acceptanceQuestion: Based only on the rendered public homepage, would this fictionalized Abby Covert information-architecture lens accept the page for publication?
nonEndorsementBoundary: This is an isolated advisory simulation using a fictionalized lens derived from Abby Covert's public work. It is not her participation, quotation, endorsement, approval, or actual sign-off.
critique: Pass. Within the opening screen, the role title, plain-language promise, short explanation, and two immediate actions establish a coherent practice centered on technical project management, product operations, implementation, and durable documentation. The following “Choose what you need to see” section gives a hurried hiring reader three distinct, question-oriented routes to role-fit evidence, case studies, and the current resume. The proof points then supply fast credibility before the six consistently structured projects demonstrate one operating practice across different settings. Capabilities and “How I work” earn their later placement by synthesizing those examples into a reusable model rather than introducing an unrelated taxonomy. Desktop scanning is strong, and the mobile sequence preserves the same hierarchy and actions, although the complete project list creates a long middle scroll.
strengths: The opening copy explains both what Jamie does and what becomes usable, giving a new visitor a practical mental model without requiring interpretation of a résumé-style title alone.
“Assess role fit,” “Inspect the work,” and “Review the current resume” are distinct, accurately described paths framed around visitor needs rather than the site's internal organization.
The progression from concise proof points to selected projects, capabilities, working method, and contact forms a coherent evidence hierarchy; each major section advances the hiring question.
Project cards use repeated labels, dates, scope summaries, and explicit case-study links, making varied civic, commercial, and community work legible as one practice.
Mobile retains the essential framing, route choices, evidence, résumé action, and contact action without changing the information model.
constructiveCriticism: Unify the three visible names for the role-fit route—“Technical Operations,” “See role-fit evidence,” and “Assess role fit.” The smallest useful revision is to choose one visitor-facing label, such as “Role-fit evidence,” and reuse it in the navigation, hero, and start-here section so a rushed reader does not have to infer that the labels are equivalent.

On mobile, six full project cards separate the opening decision routes from the capabilities and working-method synthesis by a substantial scroll. Add one compact “Jump to capabilities and approach” link beside “View all work” to preserve access to the mental model without removing evidence.
